title: Report a committed Supervisor change when a later VKS update is rejected
prompt:
Complete `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module for one coordinated vSphere Supervisor namespace and VKS Cluster change.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. Their vCenter contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 release commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2` and `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_update`. The VKS routes are separately named Kubernetes resource operations and must not be presented as VMware operationIds.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the protected manifest prerequisite on the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` module version `13.5.0.25380678`; it loads the real `VMware.Bindings.vSphere.Api.IVcenterNamespacesInstancesApi` binding and model types. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, bindings, specifications, or harness tools. Use the supplied genuine binding for vCenter and `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` for Kubernetes. Do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, raw sockets, or a live VMware endpoint.

Preserve and export only this function:

`Invoke-VcfVksCoordinatedChange -NamespaceApi <IVcenterNamespacesInstancesApi> -KubernetesBaseUri <string> -KubernetesToken <string> -Supervisor <string> -Namespace <string> -ClusterName <string> -ClusterClass <string> -NamespaceDescription <string> -TargetVersion <string> [-SkipCertificateCheck]`

Validate every scalar input before traffic. Names, class, description, version, and token must be nonblank. Reject CR or LF in the bearer token. `KubernetesBaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with root path and no credentials, query, or fragment. The client must not follow redirects.

The workflow is ordered and has two preflights followed by two changes:

1. Call the genuine binding method `VcenterNamespacesInstancesGetV2($Namespace)` exactly once. Require a non-null response whose Supervisor is an ordinal, case-sensitive match and whose config status is `RUNNING`.
2. Send a bodyless Kubernetes GET for the exact named `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` Cluster. Require matching namespace, name, topology class, and a nonblank topology version.
3. Construct a genuine `VcenterNamespacesInstancesUpdateSpec`, set only its `Description`, and call `VcenterNamespacesInstancesUpdate($Namespace, $spec)` exactly once. The fixture commits this change and returns HTTP 204.
4. Send one Kubernetes JSON merge PATCH for the Cluster's target topology version. The fixture deliberately rejects this later change with HTTP 422 and a sensitive response marker.

A Kubernetes operational non-success must not erase knowledge of an earlier committed change. For the fixture outcome, return one object with exactly `OverallStatus`, `NamespaceChange`, and `ClusterChange`. `OverallStatus` is `Failed`. `NamespaceChange` has exactly `OperationId`, `Namespace`, `Status`, and `Changed`, with operationId `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_update`, status `Succeeded`, and changed true. `ClusterChange` has exactly `OperationKey`, `Namespace`, `Name`, `Status`, `Changed`, and `HttpStatus`, with operation key `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2:namespaced-clusters:patch`, status `Failed`, changed false, and integer status 422. Do not throw for that HTTP 422. Do not include credentials, response bodies, the sensitive marker, or underlying transport exception text in output or errors.

Wire shape is exact. Percent-encode every dynamic path value as one UTF-8 RFC 3986 segment. Send `Accept: application/json` on all four requests. The genuine binding must send exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header only to vCenter; send exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <KubernetesToken>` header only to Kubernetes. GETs have no body, Content-Type, or query. The vCenter PATCH has media type `application/json` (the installed generated binding emits the exact header `application/json; charset=utf-8`) and a body containing exactly `description`. Leave `resource_spec`, `access_list`, `storage_specs`, `vm_service_spec`, `content_libraries`, `network_spec`, `zones`, `edges`, and `infrastructure_policies` unset so the generated binding omits them rather than serializing null, an empty string, array, or object. The Kubernetes PATCH has exact `Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json` and body `{"spec":{"topology":{"version":"<TargetVersion>"}}}`. Omit `dryRun`, `fieldManager`, `fieldValidation`, `force`, and `pretty` entirely; never append a bare `?`.

Run `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`. The protected verifier imports the environment-provided VMware module, constructs its genuine generated vSphere binding against an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` service, generates identifiers, credentials, descriptions, versions, and the sensitive failure marker at runtime, and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. It checks exact ordered methods, raw targets, headers, bodies, omission of every unset optional, credential separation, the committed-first/rejected-later report, and the absence of extra calls or leaked failure content. The loopback mock derives its complete route allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves no other operation. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.moonshiner/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfVksCoordinatedChange/VcfVksCoordinatedChange.psm1`.
scenario: the Supervisor namespace description update commits with HTTP 204, then the VKS Cluster topology version merge patch is rejected with HTTP 422 and the returned ledger must preserve that partial-success boundary
constraint: the contract-derived loopback request log proves exact generated-binding and Kubernetes wire shapes, total omission of unset options, authentication separation, and exactly one attempt per named operation
